body:
The commit-pinned E2E gate (#1927) waits up to 240 x 30s for the triggering commit's `sha-<commit>`
image tag. That budget is deliberately larger than the producer pipeline's configured critical path
(95 minutes), so a slow build cannot red-light an innocent PR.

The gap: the resolver has no signal from the paired build run. If that run FAILS early, the resolver
still sleeps out its whole budget before refusing, so a broken build costs ~2 hours of wall-clock
before the hard red appears. The verdict is correct - it refuses rather than testing the wrong image -
but the latency is bad enough that people will be tempted to bypass the gate, which is how a good gate
gets switched off.

Fix shape: poll the paired dev-image run's conclusion alongside the tag, and abort early with a
distinct message when that run reaches a terminal failure. Keep the long budget for "still building";
shorten only "will never arrive".

Deliberately NOT done in the #1927 PR: it is a behaviour change with its own failure mode (a
mis-identified paired run would abort a legitimate wait), and that PR was already large. Raised by the
independent pre-merge re-review of PR #1941.
title: E2E resolver waits its full ~2h budget even when the paired dev-image build has already failed
